arxiv-2111-07348.title: Invariant Risk Minimisation for Cross-Organism Inference: \titlebreak Substituting Mouse Data for Human Data in Human Risk Factor Discovery These authors contributed equally
arxiv-2111-07348.creator: Odhran ODonoghue, Paul Duckworth, Giuseppe Ughi, Linus Scheibenreif, Kia Khezeli, Adrienne Hoarfrost, Samuel Budd, Patrick Foley, Nicholas Chia, John Kalantari, Graham Mackintosh, Frank Soboczenski, Lauren Sanders
arxiv-2111-07348.description: Abstract Human medical data can be challenging to obtain due to data privacy concerns, difficulties conducting certain types of experiments, or prohibitive associated costs. In many settings, data from animal models or in-vitro cell lines are available to help augment our understanding of human data. However, this data is known for having low etiological validity in comparison to human data.

arxiv-2203-03247.title: Adaptive quantum codes: constructions, applications and fault tolerance
arxiv-2203-03247.creator: AKSHAYA J
arxiv-2203-03247.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by AKSHAYA J. KEYWORDS: Quantum error correction, Channel-adapted codes, Fault tolerance A major obstacle towards realizing a practical quantum computer is the ‘noise’ that arises due to system-environment interactions. While it is very well known that quantum error correction (QEC) provides a way to protect against errors that arise due to the noise affecting the system, a ‘perfect’ quantum code requires atleast five physical qubits to observe a noticeable improvement over the no-QEC scenario.

arxiv-2307-08412.title: A Privacy-Preserving Blockchain-based E-voting System
arxiv-2307-08412.creator: Arnab Mukherjee, Souvik Majumdar, Anup Kumar Kolya Saborni Nandi
arxiv-2307-08412.description: Abstract Within a modern democratic nation, elections play a significant role in the nation’s functioning. However, with the existing infrastructure for conducting elections using Electronic Voting Systems (EVMs), many loopholes exist, which illegitimate entities might leverage to cast false votes or even tamper with the EVMs after the voting session is complete.

arxiv-2309-07712.title: Normalized factorial moments of spatial distributions of particles in high multiplicity events: A Toy model study
arxiv-2309-07712.creator: Sheetal Sharma, Salman K. Malik, Zarina Banoo, Ramni Gupta
arxiv-2309-07712.description: Abstract In ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions a strongly interacting complex system of quarks and gluons is formed. The nature of the system so created and the mechanism of multi-particle production in these collisions may be revealed by studying the normalized factorial moments ( F q F_{{\rm{q}}} ) as function of various parameters.

arxiv-2504-10360.title: Reactive power flow optimization in AC drive systems
arxiv-2504-10360.creator: Sanjay Chandrasekaran, Catalin Arghir, Pieder Jörg, Florian Dörfler, Silvia Mastellone
arxiv-2504-10360.description: Abstract This paper explores a limit avoidance approach in the case of modulation (input) and current (output) constraints with the aim of enhancing system availability of AC drives. Drawing from the observation that, in a certain range of reactive power, there exists a trade-off between current and modulation magnitude, we exploit this freedom and define a constrained optimization problem.

arxiv-2511-05632.title: Relativistic MOND Theory from Modified Entropic Gravity
arxiv-2511-05632.creator: A. Rostami 1 , K. Rezazadeh 2 , and M. Rostampour 1
arxiv-2511-05632.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by A. Rostami 1 , K. Rezazadeh 2 , and M. Rostampour 1. We derive a relativistic extension of Modified Newtonian Dynamics (MOND) within the framework of entropic gravity by introducing temperature-dependent corrections to the equipartition law on a holographic screen. Starting from a Debye-like modification of the surface degrees of freedom and employing the Unruh relation between acceleration and temperature, we obtain modified Einstein equations in which the geometric sector acquires explicit thermal corrections.

pmc-10574720.title: Biocontrol of Botrytis cinerea as Influenced by Grapevine Growth Stages and Environmental Conditions
pmc-10574720.creator: Valeria Altieri, Vittorio Rossi, Giorgia Fedele, Gabriella Cirvilleri, Paolo Cortesi, Cecilia Mónaco
pmc-10574720.description: The growth of four commercial biocontrol agents (BCAs: Bacillus amyloliquefaciens (BAD), Aureobasidium pullulans (APD), Metschnikowia fructicola (MFN), and Trichoderma atroviride (TAS)) was evaluated using turbidimetric assays on artificial substrates mimicking the chemical berry composition at four stages: pea-sized berries, veraison, softening, and ripe berries. The response of BCA growth differed among BCAs.

pmc-11041814.title: Dexmedetomidine vs Dexamethasone as an Adjuvant to Levobupivacaine in Ultrasound-Guided Transversus Abdominis Plane Block for Postoperative Analgesia in Patients Undergoing Total Abdominal Hysterectomies
pmc-11041814.creator: Jyoti Sinha, Abhimanyu Singh Pokhriyal, Veena Asthana, Ruchira Nautiyal
pmc-11041814.description: BackgroundIn the postoperative period, open total abdominal hysterectomy (TAH) surgeries induce considerable pain. Multimodal strategies are being used to alleviate pain.ObjectivesThis study aimed to examine the efficacy and safety of dexamethasone and dexmedetomidine as an adjuvant to levobupivacaine in ultrasound-guided transversus abdominis plane (TAP) blocks for postoperative pain in TAH patients.

pmc-11372109.title: Inhibition of BCAT1-mediated cytosolic leucine metabolism regulates Th17 responses via the mTORC1-HIF1α pathway
pmc-11372109.creator: Yeon Jun Kang, Woorim Song, Su Jeong Lee, Seung Ah Choi, Sihyun Chae, Bo Ruem Yoon, Hee Young Kim, Jung Ho Lee, Chulwoo Kim, Joo-Youn Cho, Hyun Je Kim, Won-Woo Lee
pmc-11372109.description: Branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs), particularly leucine, are indispensable AAs for immune regulation through metabolic rewiring. However, the molecular mechanism underlying this phenomenon remains unclear. Our investigation revealed that T-cell receptor (TCR)-activated human CD4+ T cells increase the expression of BCAT1, a cytosolic enzyme responsible for BCAA catabolism, and SLC7A5, a major BCAA transporter.

pmc-11479260.title: Intelligent Method of Identifying the Nonlinear Dynamic Model for Helicopter Turboshaft Engines
pmc-11479260.creator: Serhii Vladov, Arkadiusz Banasik, Anatoliy Sachenko, Wojciech M Kempa, Valerii Sokurenko, Oleksandr Muzychuk, Piotr Pikiewicz, Agnieszka Molga, Victoria Vysotska, Stefano Lenci
pmc-11479260.description: This research focused on the helicopter turboshaft engine dynamic model, identifying task solving in unsteady and transient modes (engine starting and acceleration) based on sensor data. It is known that about 85% of helicopter turboshaft engines operate in steady-state modes, while only around 15% operate in unsteady and transient modes.

pmc-11484174.title: Modulating the pH dependent photophysical properties of green fluorescent protein†
pmc-11484174.creator: David P. Broughton, Chloe G. Holod, Angelica Camilo-Contreras, Darcy R. Harris, Scott H. Brewer, Christine M. Phillips-Piro
pmc-11484174.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The photophysical properties of the β-barrel superfolder green fluorescent protein (sfGFP) arise from the chromophore that forms post-translationally in the interior of the protein. Specifically, the protonation state of the side chain of tyrosine 66 in the chromophore, in addition to the network of hydrogen bonds between the chromophore and surrounding residues, is directly related to the electronic absorbance and emission properties of the protein.

pmc-11494485.title: Targeted Genetic Sequencing Analysis of 223 Cases of Pseudomyxoma Peritonei Treated by Cytoreductive Surgery and Hyperthermic Intraperitoneal Chemotherapy Shows Survival Related to GNAS and KRAS Status
pmc-11494485.creator: Jane Gibson, Reuben J. Pengelly, Amatta Mirandari, Konstantinos Boukas, Sophia Stanford, Thomas Desmond Cecil, Faheez Mohamed, Sanjeev Paul Dayal, Alexios Tzivanakis, Brendan John Moran, Alex Mirnezami, Norman John Carr, Sarah Ennis
pmc-11494485.description: Background and AimPseudomyxoma peritonei (PMP) is an unusual condition with unique behaviour caused by a mucinous neoplasm, usually arising from the appendix. The aim of this study was to evaluate the prevalence of genomic alterations in clinical specimens of PMP using a targeted assay and correlate the findings with clinical, pathological and outcome data.

pmc-11504003.title: Altered PLCβ/IP3/Ca2+ Signaling Pathway Activated by GPRCs in Olfactory Neuronal Precursor Cells Derived from Patients Diagnosed with Schizophrenia
pmc-11504003.creator: Zuly A Sánchez-Florentino, Bianca S Romero-Martínez, Edgar Flores-Soto, Luis M Montaño, Bettina Sommer, Marcela Valdés-Tovar, Jesús Argueta, Eduardo Calixto, Arnoldo Aquino-Gálvez, Manuel Castillejos-López, Héctor Serrano, Juan C Gomez-Verjan, Germán O López-Riquelme, Gloria A Benítez-King, Ruth Jai
pmc-11504003.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Background: Schizophrenia (SZ) is a multifactorial chronic psychiatric disorder with a worldwide prevalence of 1%. Altered expression of PLCβ occurs in SZ patients, suggesting alterations in the PLCβ/IP3/Ca2+ signaling pathway. This cascade regulates critical cellular processes in all cell types, including the neuronal lineage; however, there is scarce evidence regarding the functionality of this transduction signaling in neuronal cells derived from SZ patients. Objective: We evaluated the functionality of the PLCβ/IP3/Ca2+ pathway in olfactory neuronal precursor cells (hONPCs) obtained from SZ patients.

pmc-12433489.title: Cryptosporidium and cryptosporidiosis: An update of Asian perspectives in humans, water and food, 2015–2025
pmc-12433489.creator: Shahira Abdelaziz Ali Ahmed, Sonia Boughattas, Mohammad Reza Mahmoudi, Huma Khan, Simuzar Mamedova, Ardra Namboodiri, Frederick R. Masangkay, Panagiotis Karanis
pmc-12433489.description: Cryptosporidium species are increasingly recognized as significant enteric pathogens, particularly within developing nations, where they pose serious public health challenges. This systematic review and meta-analysis examine a decade of research (2015–2025) to map the epidemiological footprint of Cryptosporidium across Asia, incorporating 228 studies from 28 countries and analyzing a collective sample of 327,783 specimens collected from humans, water, and food.

pmc-12567753.title: Laboratory Analysis of Backpack Design and Walking Gradient Effects on Gait Kinetics and Kinematics
pmc-12567753.creator: Timothy Grigg, Natalia Kabaliuk, Sibi Walter, Jared Coburn
pmc-12567753.description: Background: Heavy backpacks are carried by hikers during prolonged trekking trips. A backpack’s design could impact a hiker’s gait kinematics and kinetics. Objective: We aimed to assess the impact of backpack designs on lumbar extension (LE) and centre of pressure (COP) during walking.

pmc-12676699.title: Delayed-onset parkinsonism is common after isolated striatal infarcts
pmc-12676699.creator: Hedda Holm, Espen Dietrichs, Juho Joutsa, James P. Connelly, Christian G. Lund, Mona Skjelland, Vidar Gundersen, Silje Bjerknes
pmc-12676699.description: BackgroundWhile case studies have suggested that only a minority of patients with putaminal lesions develop parkinsonism, existing data are limited by involvement of adjacent brain regions, brief follow-up period, and lack of systematic imaging. As a result, the true incidence and nature of parkinsonism following isolated striatal infarcts remain unknown.

pmc-13132952.title: Stability and Change in Wellbeing Throughout Adolescence and Its Relationship with Life Events: A Longitudinal Twin Study
pmc-13132952.creator: Eirunn Skaug, Trine Waaktaar, Svenn Torgersen
pmc-13132952.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Wellbeing—the balance of positive and negative affect and life satisfaction—is closely tied to mental health. However, the sources of stability and change and how life events shape wellbeing are not well understood. Data from the Oslo University Adolescent and Young Adult Project (2,879 individuals from 1,483 families) provided wellbeing and life‑event data across three waves ~ 2 years apart (ages 12–18 at Wave 1).

pmc-13202499.title: RobInHood: a robotic chemist in a fume hood
pmc-13202499.creator: Louis Longley, Francisco Munguia-Galeano, Yushu Han, Rob Clowes, Sriram Vijayakrishnan, Adam Edwards, Gabriella Pizzuto, Hatem Fakhruldeen, Andrew Cooper
pmc-13202499.description: Fume hoods protect chemists and the environment from hazardous vapours and airborne substances produced during experiments. They are standard in chemistry laboratories worldwide. However, fume hoods were designed for manual chemistry, and there are still relatively few robotic systems designed to operate within these inherently confined spaces.

pmc-13246635.title: Persistence, chronicity, and recurrence of infection-associated urticaria following viral infections in children and adults: a systematic review
pmc-13246635.creator: Saad Alhumaid, Sara Mohammad Alshehri, Zainah Sabr, Fatima A. Aborshaid, Sundus Noorsaeed, Ashwag A. Alsaidalani, Shorooq Shwgi Banjar, Karimah Aljasem, Fai A. pmc-13246635.description: BackgroundViral infections are recognized triggers of acute urticaria; however, the long-term outcomes of infection-associated urticaria, including persistence, recurrence, and progression to chronic disease, remain incompletely characterized.ObjectiveTo systematically review the available evidence on the persistence, chronicity, and recurrence of infection-associated urticaria following viral infections in children and adults.

pmc-13450847.creator: Younes Valibeigi, Abouzar Kaboudian, Flavio Fenton, Gil Bub, Marc Birtwistle, Anna Grosberg, Marc Birtwistle, Anna Grosberg, Marc Birtwistle, Anna Grosberg, Marc Birtwistle, Anna Grosberg
pmc-13450847.description: ObjectiveReentrant arrhythmias are life-threatening cardiac events that are difficult to study due to limited experimental control over the complex circuit dynamics. uslaw-usc-t5-s607.title: 5 U.S.C. § 607 — Preparation of analyses
uslaw-usc-t5-s607.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t5-s607.description: United States Code, Title 5 (Government Organization And Employees); Part I (The Agencies Generally); Chapter 6 (The Analysis Of Regulatory Functions). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. In complying with the provisions of sections 603 and 604 of this title, an agency may provide either a quantifiable or numerical description of the effects of a proposed rule or alternatives to the proposed rule.
